$ xref live probe

by Alexander Panasenko · xrefcode.com
On this page
  1. Usage
  2. Arguments and options
  3. Examples
  4. Hit counts and callers of two hot functions
  5. Reading the output
  6. Limits
  7. Provenance

Count how often code runs in a live process, and who calls it: xref attaches uprobes to static code addresses (translated through the verified PIE slide), counts hits per probe, and with --callers recovers each caller's return address from .eh_frame and checks that it follows a call instruction.

Usage

xref live probe [OPTIONS] --pid <PID> <ADDR>...

Arguments and options

Arguments

<ADDR>...
Target static or runtime code addresses (0x... hex or decimal).

Options

--pid <PID>
Target process ID (must be non-zero).
--backend <BACKEND>
Kernel tracing backend (perf binary ring buffer by default; never silently falls back on EACCES). Values: perf (Primary native perf_event_open + mmap binary ring-buffer backend); tracefs (Explicit Linux tracefs (uprobe_events + isolated instances/) adapter).
default perf
--count
Explicitly request hit-count reporting (enabled by default).
--callers
Recover and verify caller return addresses using effective .eh_frame CFI.
--regs
Sample argument/return registers (rdi..r9, rax, rsp, rbp) on accepted hits.
--duration-ms <DURATION_MS>
Observation window duration in milliseconds (0..=60000, 0 runs until --until-hits, target exit, or SIGINT).
default 1000
--heartbeat-ms <MS>
Periodic progress heartbeat interval in milliseconds (1..=60000).
--group-by <KEY>
Group hits by key (ret for return site).
--json-lines
Print one JSON object per hit (va, tid, fetch, ret, mark) as it happens, on either backend and for any duration; the last line is the full report.
--mark-file <PATH>
File to tail for mark annotations.
--mark-regex <REGEX>
Regular expression to match lines in --mark-file.
--max-events <MAX_EVENTS>
Maximum accepted probe events before stopping (1..=65536). Defaults to 4096, or no limit with --duration-ms 0, so unbounded runs end on --until-hits, exit or SIGINT.
--fetch <NAME=EXPR>
Tracefs uprobe fetch argument (NAME=+OFFSET(%reg):u64); repeatable, tracefs backend only.
--filter <PREDICATE>
Tracefs numeric value predicate (rdi == 0x... or NAME > N); repeatable.
--every <EVERY>
Record every Nth matching tracefs event per probe (1..=1000000).
default 1
--first <FIRST>
Stop recording after the first N matching events per probe (1..=65536).
--until-hits <UNTIL_HITS>
Stop the session after this many accepted hits across probes (1..=65536).
--force-bin
Rejects unverified mismatches; accepted for CLI symmetry with maps/resolve.
--json
Emit structured schema_version: 1 JSON output.

Examples

The target is ripgrep 14.1.1 (rg) filtering an endless input stream, as on live maps. PIDs and runtime addresses belong to that run.

Hit counts and callers of two hot functions

Command
$ sudo xref -b rg live probe --pid 4084848 0x10b0c0 0x430060 --callers --duration-ms 500
Output
pid 4084848  starttime 1480887835  match verified_sha256  pie_slide +0x75a99f000000  alive true  changed false
backend perf  pid_isolated_bp true  elapsed 32ms/500ms  stop max_events  seeded_tids 1  dyn_tids 0  excluded_tgid 0  lost 106729 (lower_bound)
probe static 0x10b0c0  runtime 0x75a99f10b0c0  file 0x10b0c0  insn push    cfi entry_rsp+8_ra-8    fn 0x10b0c0 (-)  hits 2120
  caller ra 0x75a99f0fc5ec (static 0xfc5ec)  fn 0xfc020  call_site 0xfc5e7  verified true  hits 2120  [unwind_evidence_only_tail_call_possible]
probe static 0x430060  runtime 0x75a99f430060  file 0x430060  insn push    cfi entry_rsp+8_ra-8    fn 0x430060 (-)  hits 1976
  caller ra 0x75a99f138f67 (static 0x138f67)  fn 0x138ef0  call_site 0x138f62  verified true  hits 1976  [unwind_evidence_only_tail_call_possible]
stderr
xref: probe_ready {"backend":"perf","pid":4084848,"attached_tids":[4084848],"probes":["0x10b0c0","0x430060"]}

Reading the output

  • probe_ready on stderr: the probes are attached; what the target does after it is counted.
  • The session line: backend, elapsed time against the window, why it stopped (max_events here: the 4096-event default was reached within milliseconds, because ripgrep calls these functions for every line), and lost events the ring buffer dropped (a lower bound).
  • One block per probe: static and runtime address, the first instruction and its CFI state, the hit count, and with --callers each verified caller: return address, caller function, call site and its hits. unwind_evidence_only_tail_call_possible says the caller was found by unwinding, so a tail call in between cannot be ruled out.

Limits

  • Opening uprobes on another process needs privileged perf access (root, or capabilities and kernel.perf_event_paranoid settings that allow it).
  • Busy functions reach --max-events quickly; raise it, or bound the run with --until-hits, or sample with --every N on the tracefs backend.

Provenance

Recorded with a development build of xref after 0.4.0 on Linux x86-64, on rg = ripgrep 14.1.1 (official stripped release). Live examples ran against one ripgrep process filtering an endless input stream; commands shown with sudo ran as root. Output is unchanged except that whitespace at the end of each line and empty lines at the end of the output are removed; long outputs are cut where marked.
